name.text: Drawing the image of a triangle

questiontext.text:

generalfeedback.text:
A translation moves every point by the same vector. Add \({@T[1]@}\) to each x-coordinate and \({@T[2]@}\) to each y-coordinate:

\(A({@O1[1]@},\,{@O1[2]@}) \to A'({@g1[1]@},\,{@g1[2]@})\), \(B({@O2[1]@},\,{@O2[2]@}) \to B'({@g2[1]@},\,{@g2[2]@})\), \(C({@O3[1]@},\,{@O3[2]@}) \to C'({@g3[1]@},\,{@g3[2]@})\).

The image is the same size and shape as the object and faces the same way.

questiondescription.text:
Vectors: drawing the image under a translation

Grade 12 CBE Essential 2.2: Drag three points, or type their coordinates, to draw the image of a triangle under a translation by a column vector.

Essential

This question is adapted from Question B8 in Section B of Chapter 15 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Foundation 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: new numbers, Kenyan context, STACK randomisation, answered by dragging the image vertices or typing their coordinates, with named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: Your triangle moved by \({@col(-T)@}\), the opposite way. Add \(\mathbf{T}\): each point moves \({@T[1]@}\) across and \({@T[2]@}\) up.
You swapped the moves: the top number of \(\mathbf{T}\) is the move across.
One of your moves goes the wrong way: positive is right or up, negative is left or down.
Your image is a translation, but by \({@col(Wr)@}\), not by \(\mathbf{T}\).

\(A'\) is [[if test="okA"]]right[[else]]not right[[/if]], \(B'\) is [[if test="okB"]]right[[else]]not right[[/if]] and \(C'\) is [[if test="okC"]]right[[else]]not right[[/if]]. Every vertex moves by the same vector \(\mathbf{T}\): move the others the way the right one moved.

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="perm"]]Your three points are at the corners of the image, but with the wrong labels, so this does not score. \(A'\) means the image of A: it is where A itself goes, so each letter must be in its own place. Here A moves by \(\mathbf{T}\) to \(({@O1[1]+T[1]@},\,{@O1[2]+T[2]@})\), so that is where \(A'\) belongs. Move \(B'\) and \(C'\) the same way.[[else]]Your points moved by different vectors: A by \({@col(mvA)@}\), B by \({@col(mvB)@}\) and C by \({@col(mvC)@}\). In a translation every vertex moves by the same vector, so the image is the same triangle facing the same way. Add \({@T[1]@}\) to each x-coordinate and \({@T[2]@}\) to each y-coordinate.[[/if]]
